approach.method_basis: The Parent maintains a live population of the best accepted molecular graphs, ordered by score and then admission serial. It breeds from three preferred score bands using fragment crossover and local mutations, with the inherited continuation and retry rules. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable molecular identity and novelty checks admit a full fresh proposal pool, and a count-fingerprint Gaussian process uses correlated posterior samples to allocate the evaluation batch. Every accepted score enters the complete model archive; high-scoring offspring can survive and breed later. At exactly tied scores the current serial ordering favors older records.
approach.novelty: Give newer accepted batches priority only when survivor scores are exactly equal, while preserving serial order within each batch. This changes the deterministic retention key and keeps the existing score-band sampler. The intended route is that equally scored recent offspring can survive or reach a preferred breeding band and expose useful future neighborhoods without sacrificing a strict score decision in that local contest. The frozen-initial-cohort test removed recursive reuse; the parallel uniform-parent control changes the draw law. This test retains both recursion and the original draw law. Historical size and distance preferences selected one walk state and provide counterexamples, not a transferred rule. Only one current-Parent test of this exact recency key is proposed; preserving current scores does not guarantee later gains.

observed_bottleneck: The current Parent n-62daf219c70a sorts survivors by (-score,serial). Consequently older accepted records precede newer batches at exact score equality, including across retention and breeding-band boundaries. The completed current-profile baseline has mean 0.5956696497334577 and seed-macro population deviation 0.02659287062806747. Independent passive reconstruction of its fifteen actual histories reproduces the ticket's 4350 accepted-retention calls, 206 different same-contest survivor sets, 3498 different retained orders, 507 different immediate positive-support sets and 339 reordered pre-suggestion states out of 435. Every compared local retained score vector is identical. Further separation matters: 1336 local contests change identity-specific first-parent probabilities; at the actual pre-suggestion states, 131 change those probabilities and only 52 change positive support. Counts overlap, and the hypothetical list never becomes a future state in this audit. This documents exact-tie barriers, not future utility or guaranteed Child exposure. The supported n-4d4b5eafa8b3 recursive-feedback control lost 0.260205546950089 across all fifteen matched endpoints, satisfying the narrow prerequisite that later breeding from accepted offspring can matter. It does not establish that younger equally scored records are better. n-28dc36ed5be7 broadened survivor/core coverage yet lost all seed macros, and directly protected records never bred. The L16 exact-maximum compactness tests n-770a3cefca6a and n-d4f4384cd477 changed the same six decisions and have identical fifteen scored histories with mean loss 0.0011038146568116785; n-4341f3da1e57 changed twenty motif-distance winners and lost mean 0.0018116198229683282. These counterexamples show that equal immediate scores can lead to worse futures. They have different consumers, source Parents and concrete tie laws; none supplies a recency-retention benefit.
hypothesis: Within score-greedy live-population retention, order records by descending raw accepted score, then descending origin_batch only at exact score equality, then ascending serial within each batch, retaining the original population cap and score-quantile parent sampler.

finding_summary.headline: Recent tied survivors reach real breeding, but preserving current scores still lowers the paired mean by 0.020779.
finding_summary.insights:
Most first changes in the search come from deterministic reordering rather than stronger sampling pressure: 14 of 15 first differing parent draws occur in states with unchanged first-parent probability maps. A fixed random index can select a different tied molecule even when its marginal probability is unchanged. Later band shifts do reach real breeders, so the result is not explained by absent exposure. However, the population-cutoff route remains unused, and the two evaluated products of newly supported parents both lose to their best parents. Local descendant wins and widespread later ancestry do not identify which part of the key change causes the endpoint loss.

Immediate score equality protects a local decision, not the usefulness of future neighborhoods. The molecular assessment finds chemically distinct exact ties, reactive bond environments, questionable ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry alongside useful conventional amines and carbonyl frameworks. A newer record supplies no chemical-quality guarantee. The large loss in one decoration-hopping seed coexists with gains in its other two seeds; the very small first docking loss coexists with larger docking losses in the other seeds. These exceptions remain part of the complete result.

The single registered gain test ends with this negative conditional result. Earlier structural-retention and walk-tie failures remain separate counterexamples, and the two identical compactness panels count as one history. This experiment does not assign separate membership and ordering effects, establish chemical mediation, resolve the whole evolutionary foundation or combine with the other shared-Parent interventions.
finding_summary.results:
The new tie priority changes 3,504 of 4,350 local retained orders and 207 survivor sets while preserving every same-contest retained score vector and all 15 initial populations. At the 435 states actually used for generation, 136 first-parent probability maps and 46 support sets differ. Parents whose probability increases are used in 2,813 draws and participate in 126 evaluated products: 16 beat the best generating parent, nine tie and 101 lose. Seven raise the incumbent. All 145 records newly kept at the population cutoff remain outside later breeding support and never breed after that protection.

The mechanism activates, including real probability shifts and evaluated descendants, but the complete endpoint prediction fails. Mean final Top-1 falls from 0.595670 to 0.574891, a paired change of -0.020779 against the required +0.002. Seed changes are -0.041461, +0.001143 and -0.022017. Seven of fifteen endpoints improve and eight decline; four task means decline. Every supplied run completes and every proposal pool fills. Lower seed dispersion accompanies the lower mean.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines remain prominent; exact-score ties preserve reactive and geometrically doubtful chemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child n-03acfe1ba8af and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectories were present and read. The immutable brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, with no profile mismatch or uncovered objective. Each task has 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer evaluations; each matched task/seed has the same ten fixed initial molecule/score records and 300 distinct accepted identities. Every Child retained best exceeds its fixed initial best. The observed chemistry therefore includes useful search even where its matched Parent endpoint is higher. The Child repeatedly produces substituted indole or benzothiophene amides, nitrogen-rich fused heterocycles, linked azaaryl systems, aryl/cyclic amines and carbonyl-rich bridged rings. There are multiple chemical families across seeds, with much narrower leading series within individual seeds. In fixed task order, ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9632, 0.9678, 0.9736, 0.9851 and 0.9678; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9621, 0.9655, 0.9632, 0.9805 and 0.9575. These are incidences of SMILES text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout. Distinct identities across the respective three-seed panels are 876, 876, 875, 875 and 873; cross-seed recurrence is separate from the 300 unique accepted identities within each run. Read-only RDKit perception of all supplied trajectories supports the chemical descriptions and size summaries. No objective, affinity or synthetic-feasibility score was calculated. Many molecules have recognizable medicinal-chemistry components, including ordinary aryl halides, amides, ethers and available amines. The weak drug-likeness and questionable synthetic-plausibility readings reflect recurrent N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, cyanates, nitroso or thioformyl groups, unusual bridged rings and a cyclic cumulene, rather than an absence of rings or useful amines. Some high-scoring counterexamples avoid reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds or peroxides, and chemical plausibility does not consistently follow the supplied score gradient. The source difference is confined to recent origin_batch priority inside exact raw-score retention ties plus passive provenance diagnostics; cap, accepted archive, inherited quantile sampler and posterior/graph machinery remain present. Origin batch is an admission-history fact, not a chemical descriptor. The local contest is the actual live population plus the sequential newcomer, not the full archive. The read-only log audit joins each of the thirty task/seed trajectory leaders to its pooled, emitted and accepted records and actual scored generating parents. It also preserves representative local tie contests, actual parent draws and evaluated products. Initial records, retained population members, positive sampling support and actual selected parents are different sets. In one early equal-score indole pair, recency changes order while both first-parent probabilities remain equal; the recorded inserted-nitrogen product scores below its starting parent. Another exact tie changes a linked azaaryl parent's band probability while retaining the same local membership; its evaluated crossover product is larger and lower-scoring. A tied aryl-amine record crosses the positive-support boundary and actually participates in crossover, but the cited accepted product is the tiny fluorine molecule and is not admitted as a survivor. At a different cap contest, two equally scored methyl halides differ in retained membership while both have zero breeding probability and neither breeds later. Terminal retained-order changes have no later breeding opportunity. These deliberately selected examples distinguish order, membership, probability, support, actual breeding and accepted descendants; they are not frequencies of chemical success or activation verdicts. Passive legacy orders and probabilities in this audit reuse identical local Child contests. They are not scored alternative continuations, and local strict-score-vector preservation is not future-outcome preservation. All Child pool-size receipts show the inherited full pool; no reduced-pool or compute-saving interpretation follows. An unscored graph intermediate, a pooled offspring, an emitted proposal, an accepted scored molecule, a live survivor and a retained-best endpoint are separate observations. Chemical frequencies here describe accepted trajectories, not a census of unselected pool chemistry; unselected alternatives receive no invented labels or missing-chemistry inference. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 evaluations, not the retained best of every seed. The original chemistry reports of n-c55c3d520a2c and its identical-trajectory carry-forward n-62daf219c70a were read through the fresh evidence index; historical reproduction supplies provenance, not independent replication. This is one complete same-Parent panel with adaptive histories. Shared baselines with round19 siblings are nonindependent; this report makes no compound, additive or interaction claim with another slot. Ancestry overlaps and crossover can have two scored parents; chemical association does not isolate rank versus membership effects, identify mediation, justify a blanket preference for younger molecules, or establish a whole-foundation contribution. The five per-task sections retain every seed endpoint and its chemistry exceptions. Audits are under .slots/r0019-03-improve-L01/molecular/, including trajectory_audit.json, inspected_records.json, leader_provenance.json, retention_examples.json, identity_scope_check.json and history_molecular_sources.json. No source or supplied trajectory/log path was missing. Only Child digest/trusted-trajectory SMILES are quoted; Parent-only structures are identified by published task, seed and evaluation.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer evaluations have median 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, with a range from tiny fragments to 43-heavy-atom joined heteroaromatic material. The initial trimethoxyindole carboxanilide gives way to alkyl/methoxy-substituted fused aromatic families. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 191 has 25 heavy atoms, a fluoromethyl group, chloroaniline and an unusual four-membered nitrogen-containing fused closure. The seed-1 leader at evaluation 247 has 26 heavy atoms, an N-fluorinated indole and a pyridyl alpha-keto N-chloroamide. The seed-2 leader at evaluation 284 has 25 heavy atoms and a benzothiophene N-hydroxy aryl amide with a vinylamino substituent; it avoids N-halogen bonds. The matched Parent leaders are an N-chloroindole cumulene at seed 0/evaluation 289, an N-fluoroindole N-hydroxy pyridyl amide at seed 1/evaluation 293, and an N-chloroindole aryl diketone at seed 2/evaluation 294. Both panels therefore explore related fused aromatic/polar frameworks, with local reactivity and geometry concerns in different places.
liabilities: N-F/N-Cl/N-Br connections and the seed-0 four-membered fused nitrogen closure raise local stability or geometric questions; valid SMILES do not demonstrate preparability.
The stream includes both loss of almost all useful context in methyl halides and oversized joined heterocycles with very low observed scores.
missing_features: The evaluated leading series do not consistently offer conventional bond environments that preserve the favorable compact fused-aromatic and polar-group arrangement; the observed N-Cl gain does not establish that reactivity is required.

Useful scaffold alternatives are uneven: the benzothiophene N-hydroxyamide is a real non-N-halogen counterexample, while exact-score halogen substitutions alone do not demonstrate independent useful chemical neighborhoods.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fluoroanilide and the chloroanilide at seed 0/evaluation 13 both score 0.3051048083696145. At the source retention state for the next batch, the newer chloro record changes from passive legacy rank 1 to active rank 0 while both retain first-parent probability 0.30000000000000004. That record actually breeds the ring-expanded nitrogen product at evaluation 22, scoring 0.2725382860570979; an order change and a real descendant do not guarantee improvement. Seed 1/evaluation 221, the non-N-chlorinated alpha-ketoamide, scores 0.43333853142324064; its logged append-atom product at evaluation 247 scores 0.4624615253670981. Here the observed gain accompanies adding a chemically questionable N-Cl bond. The N-F and N-Br alpha-ketoimine variants at evaluations 228 and 265 both score 0.44080749154906895 despite distinct halogen environments. Conversely, the enlarged joined heterocycle at seed 0/evaluation 48 scores 2.54236269079709e-09, and seed-1 methyl fluoride/methyl bromide both score 3.0022306134138205e-20. At retention_id 67 the newer methyl fluoride is retained over methyl bromide, but both local first-parent probabilities are zero and neither breeds later in the complete log. The visible gradient rewards a particular compact aromatic/polar arrangement, not size, halogen count, recency or plausible synthesis alone. Seed 0 has a higher Child endpoint while seeds 1 and 2 have higher Parent endpoints. Complete matched retained-best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.4126819838532174 / 0.39405142067435733; seed 1: 0.4624615253670981 / 0.47411701813450596; seed 2: 0.4163503402962837 / 0.438972502037081. These endpoint associations do not identify a chemical mediator.

per_task.generated_character: Evaluated offspring have median 32 heavy atoms and four rings; some joined products reach 96 heavy atoms. Seed 0/evaluation 298 is a 31-heavy-atom nitrogen-rich fused dione linked through nitrogen to an azaaryl region, with formyl and thioformyl groups. Seed 1/evaluation 291 is a 34-heavy-atom linked pyridyl/phenyl/aza-fused carbonyl system with an amino linker, propargyl and cyanate substituents and carbon-bound halogens. Seed 2/evaluation 260 is a 30-heavy-atom arylmethylamine/pyridine carrying alkenyl groups, a nitroso group and a benzofused cyclic peroxide/ether. The Parent seed-0 leader at evaluation 281 is a compact but unusual cross-linked azaheterocyclic carbonyl/thione system with O-F and a halomethyl ether. Parent seeds 1 and 2 lead with linked azaaryl cyanate/carbonyl and peroxide-bearing arylamine families respectively. Recognizable aromatic linking chemistry coexists with groups that make a blanket plausible-synthesis reading inappropriate.
liabilities: The seed-2 peroxide and nitroso group, seed-1 cyanate and seed-0 aldehyde/thioformyl and nitrogen linkages warrant synthetic and stability scrutiny beyond graph parsing.
Large joined multiaryl products and small floor-scoring fragments both expend accepted observations; ring-rich output does not imply useful scaffold coverage.
missing_features: The evaluated Child leaders do not reproduce the exceptionally high Parent seed-0 arrangement, while gains in the other seeds retain different families; useful heteroaromatic organization remains family- and seed-dependent.

Conventional local alternatives near the favorable linked heteroaromatic structures remain incomplete: peroxide-free relatives exist, but nitroso, cyanate, thioformyl or other reactive groups persist in leading output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The small fused dione at seed 0/evaluation 23 scores 0.5093370681605975, and propyne at evaluation 279 is at 0.5. The 96-heavy-atom seed-0 assembly at evaluation 53 scores 0.5628212450028556, so extra rings and size do not recover the highest observed chemistry. The seed-1 methoxy and vinyl-ether relatives at evaluations 108 and 128 tie exactly at 0.6125348559288275. per_task.generated_character: Evaluated offspring have median 30 heavy atoms and four rings. The best examples combine two aromatic regions with available aliphatic amines. Seed 0/evaluation 199 has 27 heavy atoms: a methoxyaryl region incorporated into an unsaturated 11-membered nitrogen ring and a halogenated benzyl substituent with benzylic chloride. Seed 1/evaluation 241 has 34 heavy atoms, a substituted cyclic diamine/aminal, a fused oxygen ring, a phenol and halogenated biaryl material. Seed 2/evaluation 252 has 31 heavy atoms, a densely bridged oxygen-containing aryl system and an aminoalkyl N-hydroxy cyclic diamine. The Parent leaders include a flexible diaryl tertiary amine at seed 0/evaluation 284, an aminoalkyl pyrrolidine at seed 1/evaluation 261, and a pyrrolidine/benzothiophene-derived biaryl at seed 2/evaluation 241. Both panels have useful accessible amine environments; the Child's complex bridges and aminals are not evidence of better medicinal chemistry.
liabilities: Benzylic chloride, N-hydroxy/aminal connections, crowded bridges and unspecified stereochemistry complicate stability and synthesis; neither supplied scores nor RDKit validity demonstrate affinity or a viable route.
The trajectories contain potentially stereogenic saturated and benzylic centres while explicit stereochemical assignment is absent; neutral SMILES do not imply that the available amines are nonbasic.
missing_features: The evaluated output does not consistently preserve the useful available-amine/aromatic arrangement through crossover; a recorded pair of complex supported parents can yield almost no molecular context.

Resolved stereochemical identities and convincing geometric alternatives to the dense bridged or aminal leaders are absent from these records; conventional cyclic-amine Parent examples and the high-scoring dechlorinated Child are counterexamples to any requirement for exotic connectivity.

This is an observed product of an affected breeder, not evidence that gained support carries favorable chemistry. Complete matched retained-best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.9999975918762773 / 0.9999989177995104; seed 1: 0.9885325450326038 / 0.9969753164881906; seed 2: 0.9907424032000932 / 0.9999934235240012. per_task.generated_character: Evaluated offspring have median 31 heavy atoms, five rings and comparatively little halogen substitution. The 34-heavy-atom seed-0 leader at evaluation 271 joins diaryl ether material to a bridged nitrogen/carbonyl framework with an N-N/C=N segment. The 30-heavy-atom seed-1 leader at evaluation 238 links a propylquinoline to a pyrazole-fused eight-membered carbonyl/amine ring. The 32-heavy-atom seed-2 leader at evaluation 267 links a propylquinoline to a bridged dicarbonyl and an N-O-containing ring; its perceived cycle basis includes 11-membered cycles. These are connected carbonyl/heteroaromatic architectures rather than an absence of ring complexity. The Parent leaders likewise contain diaryl or quinoline regions joined to N/O carbonyl rings: seed 0/evaluation 293, seed 1/evaluation 278 and seed 2/evaluation 261. Both Child and Parent offer recognizable lactam chemistry alongside closures whose practical geometry and synthesis are not established.
liabilities: N-N/C=N segments, N-O closures and dense bridge relationships make graph validity an incomplete account of chemical feasibility.

Potentially stereogenic bridge and saturated centres lack specified stereochemistry, while the flatter seed-1 heteroaromatic leader is a counterexample to treating every leading structure as stereochemically unresolved.
missing_features: The favorable connection of aromatic and carbonyl-rich regions is not consistently retained in simpler or larger products; the visible gradient supports arrangement and context, not a universal ring-count or molecular-size target.

The evaluated leaders do not provide experimentally or geometrically established versions of the medium-ring and bridged topologies; the near-leading dione without an N-O bond shows that a reactive-looking linkage is not required for the observed neighborhood.

per_task.generated_character: Evaluated offspring have median 27 heavy atoms and four rings, with extensive fluorination and nitrogen/carbonyl heterocyclic chemistry. Seed 0/evaluation 217 has 28 heavy atoms: a fluorinated anisole, fused imino/carbonyl nitrogen core, N-F bond, fluoromethyl substituent and saturated four-membered nitrogen ring. Seed 1/evaluation 292 has 30 heavy atoms: phenol/fluoroaryl substitution, an N-fluorinated fused dione and a multiply fluorinated tetrahydrofuran-like ring with several unassigned potential stereocentres. The non-N-halogen seed-2 leader remains geometrically questionable; removing one reactive bond class does not establish overall chemical quality.
Tiny or enlarged products can lose the favorable molecular context, and the late hydroxyl analogue shows that even a familiar functional-group substitution can accompany a severe observed score drop.

Explicit stereochemical identities are missing for the multiply substituted saturated rings, especially the fluorinated oxygen ring; the record does not demonstrate that enumeration would improve the supplied score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This chemical gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is carried forward through the identical published trajectories of n-62daf219c70a; that historical reproduction is not independent evidence. Current observations are from n-03acfe1ba8af versus n-62daf219c70a on the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile. The current condition changes recent-batch ordering only inside exact raw-score retention ties, with the inherited cap, sampler, full pool, accepted-label predictor and graph operators retained. The chemistry describes accepted output and inspected provenance, not unselected pool labels or a whole-foundation contribution. Leading series repeatedly change halogen placement, short substituents and carbonyl-adjacent or ring connections. Observed exact ties include aryl-fluoro versus aryl-chloro amides, methyl versus vinyl ethers, distinct carbonyl-ring arrangements and different allocations of carbon-bound versus nitrogen-bound halogens. Real products of affected breeders include lower-scoring expanded rings, enlarged linked aromatics and a tiny fluorine fragment. Different seeds also yield distinct useful families, and every retained best exceeds its initial best; this is not structural collapse or failure to generate novelty.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply chemically independent useful alternatives within the leading family; exact scalar-score ties can hide substantial differences in bond environment.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Seek useful chemically distinct descendants using task-local feedback, and assess their actual structures rather than treating molecular age, new strings or equal scalar scores as chemical equivalence. These examples do not authorize a new age window, tolerance, structural tie rule or parameter rescue of the bounded retention experiment. They do not separate membership from rank effects, establish chemical mediation, or imply that missing evaluated alternatives never appeared in the full pool.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
